triplets.head: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs)
triplets.tail: Overproduce collagen and crosslink it via LOXL2, creating dense fibrotic barriers that physically prevent T cell infiltration

triplets.head: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs)
triplets.tail: Secrete CXCL12 that diverts CD8+ T cells away from tumor

triplets.head: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs)
triplets.tail: Recruit immunosuppressive cells (monocytes, MDSCs, Tregs) via IL-8, CCL2, IL-6, TGF-β

triplets.head: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs)
triplets.tail: Polarize macrophages to M2 phenotype

triplets.head: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs)
triplets.tail: Induce tolerogenic dendritic cells via IL-6/STAT3/IDO pathway which depletes tryptophan and generates kynurenine

triplets.head: ecm-myCAF subtype
triplets.tail: Upregulates PD-1 and CTLA-4 on Tregs, contributing to checkpoint inhibitor resistance

triplets.head: pan-CAF subtype
triplets.tail: Expresses CXCL12, CXCL14, IL-6 associated with ICB resistance

triplets.head: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs)
triplets.tail: At least 20

triplets.head: myCAF (myofibroblastic CAF)
triplets.tail: Matrix remodeling, ECM deposition, collagen barriers, physical immune exclusion

triplets.head: myCAF
triplets.tail: ACTA2, TAGLN

triplets.head: iCAF (inflammatory CAF)
triplets.tail: Cytokine/chemokine secretion, recruit MDSCs and Tregs, metabolic support via glycolytic reprogramming

triplets.head: iCAF
triplets.tail: IL6, CXCL12, PDGFRA

triplets.head: apCAF (antigen-presenting CAF)
triplets.tail: Express MHC-II and present antigens but induce Treg activation rather than CTL activation

triplets.head: apCAF
triplets.tail: MHC-II, CD74

triplets.head: CXCL13+ CAF
triplets.tail: Promote B cell adhesion and antibody production, co-localize with B cell aggregates within TLS in nasopharyngeal cancer

triplets.head: CCL21+ and APOD+ CAFs
triplets.tail: Recruit T and B cells via CXCL12-CXCR4 axis within TLS in breast cancer

triplets.head: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs)
triplets.tail: Resident fibroblasts activated by TGF-β, FGF, PDGF, IL-1, IL-6

triplets.head: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs)
triplets.tail: Bone marrow MSCs, endothelial cells, adipocytes, pericytes, stellate cells

triplets.head: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs)
triplets.tail: M2-polarized TAMs deplete L-arginine via ARG1 which impairs TCR signaling

triplets.head: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs)
triplets.tail: Secrete IL-10, VEGF, and TGF-β

triplets.head: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs)
triplets.tail: Express high levels of PD-L1 to suppress T cells

triplets.head: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs)
triplets.tail: Promote angiogenesis and ECM remodeling

triplets.head: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs)
triplets.tail: Most abundant immune cells in many tumors

triplets.head: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs)
triplets.tail: Predominantly M2-polarized

triplets.head: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs)
triplets.tail: Promote lymphangiogenesis via VEGF-C; subcapsular sinus macrophages promote LN metastasis via IL-1α-STAT3

triplets.head: Myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs)
triplets.tail: Impair T cell recognition through peroxynitrite-mediated antigen modification

triplets.head: Myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs)
triplets.tail: Secrete ARG1, IDO, TGF-β, ROS, iNOS

triplets.head: Myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs)
triplets.tail: Stimulate Treg expansion

triplets.head: Myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs)
triplets.tail: Promote angiogenesis, EMT, and cancer stemness

triplets.head: Regulatory T cells (Tregs)
triplets.tail: Produce adenosine via CD39/CD73 which suppresses TCR signaling

triplets.head: Regulatory T cells (Tregs)
triplets.tail: Secrete IL-10 and TGF-β

triplets.head: Regulatory T cells (Tregs)
triplets.tail: CD4+CD25+FOXP3+

triplets.head: Pericytes
triplets.tail: Recruit MDSCs, polarize macrophages to M2, suppress CD4+/CD8+ T cell proliferation via PGE2, HGF, PD-L1 upregulation

triplets.head: Pericytes
triplets.tail: Can transform into CAFs via PI3K/AKT and MEK/ERK pathways

triplets.head: Pericytes
triplets.tail: Abnormal and loosely attached in tumors causing leaky vasculature, hypoxia, and aggressiveness

triplets.head: Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs)
triplets.tail: Inhibit NK and DC activity, promote M2 polarization, increase Tregs, reduce B cell activation

triplets.head: MSC-derived exosomes
triplets.tail: Spread immunosuppressive signals and induce MDSC-to-M2 TAM differentiation

triplets.head: Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs)
triplets.tail: Can differentiate into CAFs

triplets.head: Adipocytes (Cancer-Associated)
triplets.tail: Undergo lipolysis releasing free fatty acids for tumor cell energy and membrane synthesis

triplets.head: Adipocytes (Cancer-Associated)
triplets.tail: Produce leptin which promotes proliferation and activates macrophages

triplets.head: Adipocytes (Cancer-Associated)
triplets.tail: Secrete MMPs (MMP-1, -7, -10, -11, -14) for ECM remodeling

triplets.head: Adipocytes (Cancer-Associated)
triplets.tail: Can transdifferentiate into CAFs

triplets.head: Stellate cells
triplets.tail: Activation by TGF-β transforms them to myofibroblasts that deposit ECM causing desmoplasia characteristic of PDAC

triplets.head: Hepatic stellate cells
triplets.tail: Suppress NK cell function via CXCL12 secretion enabling dormant metastatic cells to reawaken

triplets.head: Pancreatic stellate cells
triplets.tail: Undergo lipid metabolic shift and secrete lysophosphatidylcholine to support PDAC proliferation via AKT

triplets.head: Endothelial cells (Tumor-Associated)
triplets.tail: Express immune checkpoints PD-L1, PD-L2, B7-H3, IDO to suppress T cells

triplets.head: Endothelial cells (Tumor-Associated)
triplets.tail: Irregular shape, cytoplasmic projections, gaps, leaky architecture impairing drug delivery and promoting hypoxia

triplets.head: Endothelial cells (Tumor-Associated)
triplets.tail: Support formation of tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) linked to better immunotherapy responses

triplets.head: Lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs)
triplets.tail: Cross-present tumor antigens without co-stimulation inducing T cell dysfunction and apoptosis

triplets.head: Lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs)
triplets.tail: Major route for tumor cell dissemination to lymph nodes via VEGF-C/VEGFR3 signaling

triplets.head: CD8+ cytotoxic T cells
triplets.tail: Progressive transition from TCF1+ progenitor at tumor margin to TIM-3+ terminally exhausted in tumor core

triplets.head: CD8+ T cell exhaustion
triplets.tail: TOX/OX40-driven epigenetic reprogramming

triplets.head: Natural killer (NK) cells
triplets.tail: Suppressed by TGF-β, IL-10, ROS from TAMs/MDSCs; NKp30 and NKG2D downregulated

triplets.head: Natural killer (NK) cells
triplets.tail: Platelets transfer MHC-I vesicles to circulating tumor cells shielding them from NK recognition

triplets.head: Tumor-associated neutrophils (TANs)
triplets.tail: Produce growth factors, cytokines, MMPs

triplets.head: Neutrophil Extracellular Traps (NETs)
triplets.tail: Promote proliferation, migration, EMT, immunosuppression; contribute to premetastatic niche

triplets.head: B cells
triplets.tail: Some subsets produce IL-10, TGF-β; regulatory B cells promote tolerogenic phenotypes; pathogenic IgG activates pro-metastatic signaling

triplets.head: B cells
triplets.tail: Produce antibodies, act as APCs, form TLS associated with better prognosis

triplets.head: Mast cells (TAMCs)
triplets.tail: Promote angiogenesis via tryptase and VEGF, ECM degradation via MMP-9, immunosuppression via TNF-α and PD-L1

triplets.head: Mast cells (TAMCs)
triplets.tail: Enhance DC migration/maturation, promote CD8+ T cell priming, stimulate NK cell IFN-γ via TLR activation

triplets.head: Dendritic cells (DCs)
triplets.tail: IL-6, IL-10, TGF-β block maturation producing tolerogenic DCs

triplets.head: mregDC (mature regulatory DC)
triplets.tail: Discovered by scRNA-seq

triplets.head: mregDC
triplets.tail: Simultaneously expresses maturation markers AND immunosuppressive molecules (IDO1, PD-L1), capturing antigens but suppressing rather than activating T cells

triplets.head: mregDC
triplets.tail: Found enriched in immune-excluded tumors

triplets.head: Collagen (Types I, III, IV)
triplets.tail: Overproduced by CAFs causing stiffening (desmoplasia) that blocks immune infiltration and drugs; crosslinked by LOX/LOXL2

triplets.head: Hyaluronan (HA)
triplets.tail: Increases interstitial fluid pressure, promotes migration/invasion, low MW HA activates macrophages/DCs

triplets.head: Biglycan
triplets.tail: ECM proteoglycan that stimulates TLR2/4 on macrophages and DCs skewing them toward immunosuppressive phenotypes

triplets.head: Matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs)
triplets.tail: ECM degradation facilitating invasion/metastasis; release sequestered growth factors like VEGF; promote angiogenesis

triplets.head: Exosomes/Extracellular vesicles
triplets.tail: Cancer-derived PD-L1+ exosomes suppress T cells systemically

triplets.head: Exosomes/Extracellular vesicles
triplets.tail: Form premetastatic niche; carry integrins determining organotropic metastasis

triplets.head: Hypoxia
triplets.tail: HIF-1α activation reprograms Treg metabolism, enhances adenosine production via CD39/CD73, promotes collagen crosslinking via LOX, upregulates PD-L1

triplets.head: TME acidosis
triplets.tail: pH 6.5-6.8 inhibits NFAT nuclear translocation, blunting T cell activation

triplets.head: Lactate accumulation
triplets.tail: CAFs produce lactate via glycolysis which acidifies TME and impairs T and NK cell function

triplets.head: IDO1/TDO2
triplets.tail: Deplete tryptophan and generate immunosuppressive kynurenine

triplets.head: CD39/CD73 pathway
triplets.tail: Generate adenosine on tumors and Tregs that suppresses TCR signaling

triplets.head: PD-L1
triplets.tail: On tumor/myeloid cells binds PD-1 on T cells, recruits SHP-1/SHP-2, shuts down TCR signaling

triplets.head: B7-H3
triplets.tail: Upregulated via IL-6/STAT3

triplets.head: Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS)
triplets.tail: Organized ectopic lymphoid aggregates containing T cell zones, B cell follicles, DCs, HEVs; generally associated with better prognosis and enhanced immunotherapy response

triplets.head: Rudolf Virchow
triplets.tail: 1863: First to identify leukocytes in cancerous tissue, linking inflammation and cancer

triplets.head: Stephen Paget
triplets.tail: 1889: Proposed seed and soil hypothesis - metastasis is organ-specific based on microenvironment compatibility

triplets.head: William B. Coley
triplets.tail: 1891: Coley's toxins - first deliberate immune-based cancer treatment using bacterial injections

triplets.head: Paul Ehrlich
triplets.tail: 1909: Proposed cancer immunosurveillance - immune system detects and attacks emerging cancer cells

triplets.head: Frank Macfarlane Burnet and Lewis Thomas
triplets.tail: 1949/1957: Formalized cancer immunosurveillance hypothesis - lymphocytes as sentinels

triplets.head: Judah Folkman
triplets.tail: 1971: Tumor angiogenesis hypothesis published in NEJM - tumors cannot grow >1-2mm without new blood vessels

triplets.head: Ralph Steinman
triplets.tail: 1973: Identified dendritic cells as key APCs (Nobel Prize 2011)

triplets.head: Harold Dvorak
triplets.tail: 1986: Tumors: wounds that do not heal - NEJM essay connecting angiogenesis, inflammation, ECM remodeling under one umbrella

triplets.head: Mina Bissell
triplets.tail: Late 1980s-1990s: Demonstrated ECM and tissue architecture directly control gene expression; oncogenic cells rendered non-malignant in normal microenvironment

triplets.head: Tasuku Honjo
triplets.tail: 1992: Discovery of PD-1 (Programmed Death-1)

triplets.head: James Allison
triplets.tail: 1996: Anti-CTLA-4 antibody eradicates tumors in mice - proof of concept for checkpoint blockade

triplets.head: First International Conference on TME
triplets.tail: 1995: Held at Sea of Galilee, Israel, approximately 250 participants; led to founding of ICMF

triplets.head: Hanahan and Weinberg
triplets.tail: 2000: Hallmarks of Cancer - 6 core capabilities; immune evasion NOT included

triplets.head: Schreiber, Dunn and Old
triplets.tail: 2002: Cancer immunoediting hypothesis - three phases: Elimination, Equilibrium, Escape

triplets.head: NCI
triplets.tail: 2003: TME officially declared NCI priority research area; TMEN established with 10 funded programs

triplets.head: Bevacizumab (Avastin)
triplets.tail: 2004: First anti-angiogenesis drug approved by FDA for metastatic colorectal cancer

triplets.head: Rosandra Kaplan et al.
triplets.tail: 2005: Pre-metastatic niche discovered - VEGFR1+ bone marrow progenitors prepare distant organs before cancer cells arrive

triplets.head: Paszek et al.
triplets.tail: 2005: Matrix stiffness drives malignant phenotype via mechanotransduction (integrin signaling)

triplets.head: Hanahan and Weinberg
triplets.tail: 2011: Hallmarks Next Generation - added Avoiding immune destruction and Tumor-promoting inflammation as hallmarks

triplets.head: Ipilimumab
triplets.tail: 2011: First immune checkpoint inhibitor approved by FDA for advanced melanoma

triplets.head: Pembrolizumab and nivolumab
triplets.tail: 2014: Anti-PD-1 antibodies approved by FDA

triplets.head: Tisagenlecleucel
triplets.tail: 2017: First CAR T-cell therapy approved by FDA for pediatric B-ALL

triplets.head: James Allison and Tasuku Honjo
triplets.tail: 2018: Shared Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for CTLA-4 and PD-1 discoveries

triplets.head: Grünwald et al.
triplets.tail: 2021: subTMEs discovered - spatially distinct microenvironmental states within single tumors (reactive vs deserted)

triplets.head: Beta-2 microglobulin (B2M)
triplets.tail: Loss-of-function mutations, gene deletions, or LOH impair MHC-I surface stability, rendering tumors invisible to CD8+ T cells

triplets.head: B2M loss
triplets.tail: Frequently observed in patients who initially respond to ICIs but relapse in melanoma, lung, and colorectal cancer; significantly more abundant in ICB-resistant patients

triplets.head: HLA-LOH at chromosome 6p
triplets.tail: Haplotype-specific antigen loss selectively eliminates alleles presenting immunogenic neoantigens while retaining less immunogenic variants

triplets.head: NLRC5
triplets.tail: Master transcriptional activator of MHC-I; its downregulation impairs MHC-I expression

triplets.head: Antigen processing machinery (APM) defects
triplets.tail: Mutations in TAP1/TAP2, tapasin, ERAP1/2, proteasome subunits (LMP2, LMP7, LMP10) impair antigen presentation even when MHC genes are intact

triplets.head: Tapasin loss
triplets.tail: In NSCLC correlates with impaired antigen processing and immune evasion; loss disrupts recognition by CTLs targeting survivin and CEP55

triplets.head: MHC-I epigenetic silencing
triplets.tail: Promoter hypermethylation and histone deacetylation (H3K27me3 via PRC2/EZH2) silence MHC-I genes; restorable with DNA demethylating agents

triplets.head: Immunoediting escape phase
triplets.tail: T cell-mediated immunoselection eliminates cells with strong rejection antigens, selecting for variants devoid of immunogenic neoantigens

triplets.head: d42m1 sarcoma model
triplets.tail: Escape variants lost a point mutation in Spectrin-β2 gene that originally produced a neoantigen

triplets.head: TGF-β from Tregs
triplets.tail: Suppresses cGAS-STING pathway and reduces MHC-I while increasing PD-L1 in multiple myeloma

triplets.head: Cycloastragenol (CAG)
triplets.tail: Inhibits cathepsin B reducing lysosomal degradation of MHC-I

triplets.head: Alpha-ketoglutarate (αKG)
triplets.tail: Enhances MHC-I expression via histone demethylation

triplets.head: NLRC5-Superactivator (NLRC5-SA)
triplets.tail: Boosts MHC-I expression transcriptionally

triplets.head: Cediranib
triplets.tail: Triggers STAT1 phosphorylation and IRF-1 activation upregulating MHC-I

triplets.head: SNAIL (EMT-TF)
triplets.tail: Upregulates CXCL1/CXCL2 to recruit MDSCs; suppresses CXCL10 diminishing CD8+ T cell infiltration; induces tolerogenic DCs via TSP1; generates Tregs

triplets.head: ZEB1 (EMT-TF)
triplets.tail: Upregulates PD-L1 in gastric and colorectal cancer; binds CXCL10 and CCL4 promoters to suppress expression impairing CD8+ T cell recruitment

triplets.head: TWIST1 (EMT-TF)
triplets.tail: Directly induces CCL2 to recruit macrophages; expressed at invasive front with macrophages

triplets.head: EMT
triplets.tail: Reduces surface MHC-I/HLA in breast cancer; in NSCLC mesenchymal phenotype shows decline in immunoproteasome components

triplets.head: SNAIL and ZEB1
triplets.tail: Bind E-box in CD47 promoter enabling cancer cells to evade macrophage phagocytosis

triplets.head: MFGE8
triplets.tail: Key immunosuppressive factor from mesenchymal cells that impairs CD8+ T cell proliferation and IFN-γ/TNF-α production; induces TWIST/SNAIL creating self-reinforcing loop

triplets.head: E-cadherin loss
triplets.tail: Eliminates E-cadherin-CD103 interactions that support CTL-mediated tumor lysis; fibronectin upregulation binds ILT3/LILRB4 driving myeloid suppressive phenotype

triplets.head: PD-L1
triplets.tail: ZEB1 drives PD-L1 and PD-L1 itself reinforces EMT via Ras/ERK in GBM, PI3K/AKT in nasopharyngeal cancer, SREBP-1c in RCC

triplets.head: Cancer stem cells (CSCs)
triplets.tail: Frequently exhibit MHC-I downregulation impairing CD8+ T cell recognition

triplets.head: Cancer stem cells (CSCs)
triplets.tail: Overexpress PD-L1 even at early tumor stages

triplets.head: Cancer stem cells (CSCs)
triplets.tail: Secrete TGF-β, IL-10, VEGF suppressing DC maturation, promoting Treg expansion, inhibiting T cell function

triplets.head: Wnt/β-catenin signaling
triplets.tail: Suppresses CXCL9/10 chemokine expression reducing T cell recruitment; inhibits DC infiltration and maturation

triplets.head: Cancer stem cells (CSCs)
triplets.tail: Preferentially reside in soft ECM niches within stiff tumors where nuclear softening, H3K9 demethylation, and Sox2 upregulation sustain stemness

triplets.head: CSC mechanomemory
triplets.tail: Once primed by soft niche, CSCs retain stemness-associated transcriptional programs even after transfer to different environments

triplets.head: ECM stiffness
triplets.tail: Dense aligned collagen fibers create steric blockade to T cell infiltration; stiffness raises force threshold for TCR activation

triplets.head: ECM stiffness (10-50 kPa range)
triplets.tail: Activates integrin β1/β3-FAK-Src signaling which upregulates PD-L1 and other immune checkpoint molecules

triplets.head: Stiffness-induced PD-L1 upregulation
triplets.tail: Persists even after ECM stiffness is partially normalized - a mechanical hysteresis loop mediated by YAP promoter hypomethylation and chromatin remodeling

triplets.head: Piezo1
triplets.tail: Stretch-gated ion channel; T cells exert 12-19 pN of force per TCR-pMHC bond; Piezo1-dependent Ca2+ influx enhances ZAP70 phosphorylation

triplets.head: YAP/TAZ
triplets.tail: Activated by ECM stiffness; drive expression of PD-L1, TGF-β, IL-6; link physical tumor architecture to immune evasion

triplets.head: Stiff ECM
triplets.tail: 3D bioprinted hydrogels show stiff environments significantly reduce CAR-T cell infiltration and killing capacity via hypoxia and mTORC1 activation

triplets.head: Norepinephrine (NE)
triplets.tail: Released by sympathetic nerves; via β-adrenergic receptors suppresses CTL activity, promotes M2 TAM polarization, increases VEGF/MMP

triplets.head: Acetylcholine (ACh)
triplets.tail: Released by parasympathetic nerves; impairs CD8+ T cell recruitment via nicotinic ACh receptors; context-dependent effects on tumor types

triplets.head: GABA
triplets.tail: Suppresses T cell and macrophage activation

triplets.head: Substance P (SP)
triplets.tail: Binds NK-1R promoting angiogenesis; activates mast cells; in pancreatic cancer promotes cell proliferation and migration

triplets.head: CGRP (Calcitonin Gene-Related Peptide)
triplets.tail: Promotes angiogenesis; CGRP-knockout mice show halted tumor growth

triplets.head: Neuropeptide Y (NPY)
triplets.tail: Increased NPY-positive nerves in prostate preneoplasia predict poor outcome; promotes cancer cell migration and metabolic reprogramming

triplets.head: Perineural invasion (PNI)
triplets.tail: 70% to nearly 100% of surgical specimens; an early event in pancreatic carcinogenesis

triplets.head: Schwann cells
triplets.tail: Create physical tracks (TASTs) guiding cancer cell migration; secrete TGF-β enhancing invasiveness and CCL2 recruiting macrophages

triplets.head: CXCL12/CXCR4 axis
triplets.tail: Simultaneously drives perineural invasion and creates immune-excluded phenotype by sequestering CXCR4-positive T cells

triplets.head: Chronic stress
triplets.tail: Activates CRH neurons in central amygdala leading to sympathetic fiber proliferation in breast cancer TME and tumor growth; reversed by alprazolam in mice

triplets.head: Tumor-associated nerves
triplets.tail: Express PD-L1; higher PD-L1+ nerve density correlates with worse prognosis in prostate cancer

triplets.head: Propranolol (β-blocker)
triplets.tail: Reduces PNI and increases survival in KPC mouse models when combined with chemotherapy

triplets.head: Bifidobacterium longum
triplets.tail: Enriched in melanoma ICI responders; FMT from responders improves anti-PD-L1 outcomes

triplets.head: Akkermansia muciniphila
triplets.tail: Improved anti-PD-1 efficacy in NSCLC, RCC, HCC; produces inosine that enhances antitumor immunity

triplets.head: Fusobacterium nucleatum
triplets.tail: Dual role: Fap2 binds TIGIT on NK cells inhibiting activity and recruits MDSCs; but in some contexts converts cold tumors to hot and enhances ICB

triplets.head: Clostridium scindens
triplets.tail: Produces deoxycholic acid which impairs CD8+ T cell function via Ca2+ ATPase inhibition and NFAT2 suppression

triplets.head: SCFAs (butyrate, propionate)
triplets.tail: Enhance anti-tumor immunity by inhibiting HDAC to increase CD8+ T cell cytotoxicity

triplets.head: Gut microbial molecular mimicry
triplets.tail: Bifidobacterium breve epitope SVYRYYGL mimics tumor epitope SIYRYYGL enabling cross-reactive T cell responses

triplets.head: FMT trial NCT03353402
triplets.tail: 10 PD-1-refractory melanoma patients; FMT + anti-PD-1 produced 2 partial responses + 1 complete response; increased CD8+ T cell activation

triplets.head: FMT trial NCT03341143
triplets.tail: 15 patients; FMT + pembrolizumab produced 2 PRs + 1 OR + 3 SD lasting over a year; reduced IL-8+ myeloid cells

triplets.head: Obesity
triplets.tail: WAT fibro-inflammatory progenitors secrete IL-1, IL-6, TNF under hypoxia causing systemic inflammation, ROS, DNA damage; TNF drives insulin resistance with 2x increased cancer risk

triplets.head: Aging
triplets.tail: Increased ROS, mitochondrial dysfunction, altered metabolites; accumulation of senescent cells secreting cytokines and inflammatory factors

triplets.head: Exercise
triplets.tail: Voluntary wheel running in mice shows 60% reduction in tumor incidence via epinephrine-induced NK cell tumor infiltration through IL-6; creates metabolic shield reducing free nutrients

triplets.head: Epacadostat
triplets.tail: Selective competitive IDO1 catalytic inhibitor (oral)

triplets.head: Epacadostat
triplets.tail: ECHO-301/KN-252 Phase III in advanced melanoma

triplets.head: Epacadostat
triplets.tail: Combined with pembrolizumab

triplets.head: Epacadostat
triplets.tail: FAILED: No improvement in PFS or OS vs pembrolizumab alone; trial terminated April 2018

triplets.head: Epacadostat
triplets.tail: Blocks IDO1 catalytic activity but paradoxically enhances IDO1 non-enzymatic signaling function via SHP phosphatases and PI3K p85 interaction; activates AhR creating immunosuppressive loop in pDCs

triplets.head: Linrodostat (BMS-986205)
triplets.tail: IDO1 inhibitor

triplets.head: Linrodostat
triplets.tail: Phase I/II (NCT03361228) with nivolumab; no definitive efficacy results reported

triplets.head: Telaglenastat (CB-839)
triplets.tail: Selective oral GLS1 (glutaminase 1) inhibitor

triplets.head: Telaglenastat
triplets.tail: Phase II randomized, 444 patients metastatic ccRCC: median PFS 9.2 vs 9.3 months (HR 0.94, P=0.65); ORR 31% vs 28% - no added benefit over cabozantinib alone

triplets.head: Telaglenastat
triplets.tail: Phase I/II, 118 patients: overall ORR 8.4%; CKI-naïve ccRCC subgroup ORR 24% (6/25); post-ICI melanoma 5.4%; post-ICI NSCLC 0%

triplets.head: Telaglenastat
triplets.tail: Fatigue (42.4%), nausea (39%), photophobia (32.2%)

triplets.head: DRP-104 (sirpiglenastat)
triplets.tail: Broad glutamine antagonist prodrug of DON; tumor-activated via CES1 enzyme conferring tumor selectivity

triplets.head: DRP-104
triplets.tail: Robust tumor suppression in 4/4 KEAP1-mutant PDX models; long-term growth inhibition 50+ days without resistance; KEAP1-WT tumors resistant

triplets.head: DRP-104
triplets.tail: Inhibits nucleotide synthesis (purine and pyrimidine pathways) rather than primarily glutaminolysis; distinct from CB-839

triplets.head: DRP-104
triplets.tail: Reverses T cell exhaustion, decreases Tregs, enhances CD4+ and CD8+ T cell cytokine production; significantly enhanced response to anti-PD-1 in KEAP1-mutant lung cancer

triplets.head: DRP-104
triplets.tail: Median survival tripled from 11 to 35 days as monotherapy in immunocompetent mice with KEAP1-mutant lung tumors

triplets.head: DRP-104
triplets.tail: Phase I/IIa (NCT04471415); Phase I/II with durvalumab recruiting

triplets.head: Oleclumab (MEDI9447)
triplets.tail: Anti-CD73 monoclonal antibody

triplets.head: Oleclumab
triplets.tail: Phase II unresectable Stage III NSCLC: ORR 30.0% vs 17.9% durvalumab alone; PFS HR 0.44 (95% CI 0.26-0.75); 12-month PFS 62.6% vs 33.9%

triplets.head: Oleclumab
triplets.tail: Phase II MSS-mCRC: ORR 61.5% vs 46.2% (P=0.317); median PFS 10.9 vs 11.1 months (P=0.588); no OS benefit; study terminated early

triplets.head: Oleclumab
triplets.tail: Addition to chemo-immunotherapy did not improve PFS or OS in advanced TNBC; subgroup experienced exceptional long-term responses

triplets.head: PACIFIC-9 trial
triplets.tail: Phase III double-blind randomized: durvalumab + oleclumab or durvalumab + monalizumab vs durvalumab + placebo in Stage III NSCLC; primary endpoint PFS; ongoing

triplets.head: TTX-030
triplets.tail: Anti-CD39 monoclonal antibody

triplets.head: TTX-030
triplets.tail: CD39 inhibition + anti-PD-1 achieved complete tumor eradication in 70% of mice with pre-existing tumors

triplets.head: IPH5201
triplets.tail: Phase I (NCT04261075) with 204 patients with advanced solid tumors; safety and feasibility demonstrated

triplets.head: Ciforadenant (CPI-444)
triplets.tail: A2A adenosine receptor antagonist

triplets.head: Ciforadenant
triplets.tail: First-in-human refractory RCC: median PFS 4.1 months

triplets.head: Ciforadenant
triplets.tail: Median PFS 5.8 months; 25-month OS probability 90%

triplets.head: Ciforadenant
triplets.tail: Phase Ib/2 with ipilimumab + nivolumab: safe and feasible but did not enhance activity over ipilimumab/nivolumab in frontline ccRCC

triplets.head: GS-1423
triplets.tail: Bifunctional monoclonal antibody targeting both CD73 and TGF-β pathways

triplets.head: AZD3965
triplets.tail: First-in-class oral MCT1 (monocarboxylate transporter 1) inhibitor

triplets.head: AZD3965
triplets.tail: 40 patients; RP2D 10 mg BID established; DLTs at ≥20 mg/day: asymptomatic reversible retinopathy (n=5), grade 3 cardiac troponin rise (n=1), grade 3 acidosis (n=1)

triplets.head: INCB001158 (CB-1158)
triplets.tail: Arginase inhibitor

triplets.head: INCB001158
triplets.tail: 107 patients; dose-dependent plasma arginine increases confirmed; response rates did not exceed background for given tumor types

triplets.head: INCB001158
triplets.tail: 153 patients; best ORR 19.2% in anti-PD-1-naïve HNSCC (4 PR + 1 CR out of 26); arginase-1 expression in TME did not correlate with response

triplets.head: TPST-1120
triplets.tail: PPARα antagonist targeting fatty acid metabolism

triplets.head: TPST-1120
triplets.tail: 20 patients; no grade 4-5 TRAEs or DLTs; 53% (10/19) achieved stable disease

triplets.head: TPST-1120
triplets.tail: 18 patients; ORR 20% (3/15) overall; 30% (3/10) at ≥400 mg BID; responses in 2 RCC patients previously progressed on anti-PD-1 and 1 cholangiocarcinoma

triplets.head: Metformin
triplets.tail: AMPK activator with indirect glucose/mitochondrial effects

triplets.head: Metformin
triplets.tail: 15+ active Phase II/III trials across cancer types in combination with chemotherapy, targeted therapy, and ICIs

triplets.head: Metformin
triplets.tail: Phase II in esophageal cancer: low-dose metformin reprogrammed TME immune cells increasing CD8+ T cells and decreasing Tregs

triplets.head: Bevacizumab + atezolizumab (IMbrave150)
triplets.tail: Vascular normalization + immunotherapy

triplets.head: Bevacizumab
triplets.tail: Reverses VEGF-mediated immunosuppression: improves DC maturation via NF-κB, restores ICAM-1/VCAM-1 on endothelium for T cell adhesion, reduces Tregs and MDSCs, shifts TAMs from M2 to M1

triplets.head: IMbrave150 trial
triplets.tail: Atezolizumab + bevacizumab median OS 19.2 months vs sorafenib 13.4 months (HR 0.66, p<0.001)

triplets.head: IMbrave150 trial
triplets.tail: Median PFS 6.9 months vs 4.3 months (HR 0.65, p<0.001)

triplets.head: IMbrave150 trial
triplets.tail: 18% higher ORR with combination (p<0.001)

triplets.head: IMbrave150 trial
triplets.tail: Established as standard-of-care for first-line unresectable HCC

triplets.head: T-VEC (talimogene laherparepvec)
triplets.tail: Oncolytic virus as TME reprogrammer

triplets.head: T-VEC
triplets.tail: Induces immunogenic cell death releasing tumor antigens and DAMPs; activates DCs via PAMPs; triggers type I IFN, IL-2, TNF-α cascade; converts cold tumors to hot

triplets.head: T-VEC
triplets.tail: 2015 for unresectable melanoma

triplets.head: T-VEC + ipilimumab
triplets.tail: 198 participants: ORR 39% significantly higher than monotherapy historical controls

triplets.head: T-VEC + pembrolizumab
triplets.tail: 692 participants: ORR 48.6% vs 41.3% pembrolizumab + placebo; no significant PFS or OS benefit

triplets.head: MIW815 (ADU-S100)
triplets.tail: Intratumoral STING agonist

triplets.head: MIW815 + spartalizumab
triplets.tail: Overall ORR 10.4%; 13.4% with weekly dosing; pharmacodynamic activity confirmed (increased IFNβ); efficacy deemed insufficient; study terminated early

triplets.head: STING agonists
triplets.tail: Intratumoral delivery limits applicability to accessible lesions; rapid clearance reduces sustained TME reprogramming

triplets.head: Decitabine + camrelizumab
triplets.tail: Epigenetic reprogramming + immunotherapy

triplets.head: Decitabine + camrelizumab
triplets.tail: Phase II: CR 79% (combo) vs 32% (mono); PFS 35.0 vs 15.5 months; well tolerated

triplets.head: Decitabine + camrelizumab
triplets.tail: 50 patients with R/R cHL: ORR 52%, CR rate 36%; longer PFS than anti-PD-1 monotherapy

triplets.head: Sintilimab + chidamide (HDACi)
triplets.tail: Phase Ib/II: ORR 59.5%, CR 48.6%; median DOR 25.3 months; median PFS 23.2 months; median OS 32.9 months

triplets.head: Pembrolizumab + decitabine + pralatrexate
triplets.tail: Phase I: ORR 100% (13/13 patients); median DOR 18 months

triplets.head: Epigenetic drugs
triplets.tail: Entinostat induces STAT3 acetylation in Tregs decreasing FOXP3 transcription; EZH2 inhibitor CPI-1205 shifts Tregs from immunosuppressive to proinflammatory

triplets.head: Epigenetic drugs
triplets.tail: 5-azacytidine reduces MDSC immunosuppressive function by decreasing ARG1 gene methylation

triplets.head: Epigenetic drugs
triplets.tail: HDAC6 inhibitors upregulate MHC-II and CD86 on macrophages enhancing costimulatory capacity

triplets.head: Epigenetic drugs
triplets.tail: BET inhibitors increase NKG2D ligand expression; EZH2 inhibitors enhance NK cytotoxicity and NKG2D expression

triplets.head: Radiation therapy
triplets.tail: Converting local destruction into systemic immunity via immunogenic cell death

triplets.head: Radiation therapy
triplets.tail: Releases calreticulin, ATP, HMGB1 activating DCs; activates cGAS-STING for type I IFN; increases CXCL9/10/16 for T cell recruitment; upregulates MHC-I

triplets.head: Radiation therapy
triplets.tail: Mathematical modeling predicts 6-8 Gy per fraction maximizes immunogenic cell death

triplets.head: Tebentafusp
triplets.tail: Bispecific antibody targeting gp100 (tumor) × CD3 (T cell)

triplets.head: Tebentafusp
triplets.tail: FDA-approved 2022 for uveal melanoma; 1-year OS 73% vs 59%

triplets.head: Cadonilimab
triplets.tail: Bispecific antibody targeting PD-1 × CTLA-4

triplets.head: Cadonilimab
triplets.tail: Approved in China; ORR 81.4% + chemotherapy in advanced ESCC with 97.7% disease control rate

triplets.head: Autogene cevumeran (BNT122)
triplets.tail: Individualized mRNA neoantigen vaccine

triplets.head: Autogene cevumeran
triplets.relation: Phase I result in pancreatic cancer
triplets.tail: Neoantigen-specific T cell responses in 8/16 patients; responders had significantly longer RFS (median not reached vs 13.4 months)

triplets.head: mRNA-4157/V940
triplets.tail: Personalized mRNA neoantigen vaccine

triplets.head: mRNA-4157/V940 + pembrolizumab
triplets.tail: 44% reduction in recurrence or death vs pembrolizumab alone in high-risk melanoma; Phase III V940-001 ongoing

triplets.head: FMT (Fecal Microbiota Transplantation)
triplets.tail: Microbiome-based systemic TME reprogramming

triplets.head: scRNA-seq
triplets.tail: Measures full transcriptome of individual dissociated cells; no spatial information; scale 10,000s-millions of cells

triplets.head: Spatial transcriptomics (spot-based, Visium)
triplets.tail: Measures transcriptomes within ~55 µm tissue spots; low spatial resolution

triplets.head: CosMx (NanoString/Bruker)
triplets.tail: Single-cell/subcellular spatial transcriptomics measuring 100s-6000+ genes per cell in situ

triplets.head: MERFISH
triplets.tail: Multiplexed error-robust fluorescence in situ hybridization for subcellular spatial transcriptomics

triplets.head: Xenium (10x Genomics)
triplets.tail: Single-cell resolution in situ spatial transcriptomics

triplets.head: CODEX
triplets.tail: Spatial proteomics measuring 40-60+ proteins per cell in situ

triplets.head: Imaging Mass Cytometry (IMC)
triplets.tail: Spatial proteomics for high-plex protein detection in intact tissue

triplets.head: CellChat
triplets.tail: Computational tool that quantitatively infers and analyzes intercellular communication networks from scRNA-seq data using ligand-receptor pairs

triplets.head: CXCL9:SPP1 macrophage polarity axis
triplets.tail: Identified by population-oriented scRNA-seq of 187,399 cells from 52 head and neck cancers (Science 2023)

triplets.head: CXCL9:SPP1 macrophage polarity
triplets.tail: Traditional M1/M2 macrophage paradigm which had no prognostic value in human tumors

triplets.head: CXCL9-high macrophages
triplets.tail: Produce T cell-attracting chemokine CXCL9; IFN-γ responsive; anti-tumor

triplets.head: CXCL9-high macrophages
triplets.tail: Higher T cell, B cell, and cDC1 infiltration; better patient survival across cancers

triplets.head: SPP1-high macrophages
triplets.tail: Produce osteopontin (SPP1); promote angiogenesis, ECM remodeling, immune exclusion; pro-tumor

triplets.head: SPP1-high macrophages
triplets.tail: Reduced adaptive immune infiltration; worse patient survival across cancers

triplets.head: CXCL9:SPP1 ratio
triplets.tail: High CS ratio pre-treatment in 3/5 anti-PD-1 responders; low CS ratio in 9/9 non-responders

triplets.head: CXCL9 and SPP1 expression
triplets.tail: Coordinated across entire TME - not just macrophages but also tumor cells, fibroblasts, endothelial cells, monocytes, DCs; 2,320 cell type-gene combinations associated with CS polarity

triplets.head: SPP1-high macrophages
triplets.tail: Co-localize with hypoxic tumor niches and dense ECM

triplets.head: CXCL9-high macrophages
triplets.tail: Co-localize with T cell-rich regions

triplets.head: SPP1
triplets.tail: SPP1 itself or its receptor CD44/integrins being explored as targets; shifting SPP1→CXCL9 polarity is therapeutic goal

triplets.head: Pan-cancer T cell atlas
triplets.tail: Identified 32 distinct T cell states across 16 cancer types from 308,048 transcriptomes integrating 27 scRNA-seq datasets

triplets.head: T_STR (Stress Response T cells)
triplets.tail: HSPA1A, HSPA1B (heat shock proteins)

triplets.head: T_STR
triplets.tail: Enriched in ICB non-responders; represents novel resistance mechanism distinct from exhaustion lineage

triplets.head: T_STR
triplets.tail: Detectable in lymphocyte aggregates and tertiary lymphoid structures

triplets.head: T_STR
triplets.tail: Heat shock pathway inhibition could overcome ICB resistance

triplets.head: CXCL13+ CD8+ T cells
triplets.tail: Tumor-reactive T cells that co-localize with B cell aggregates in TLS

triplets.head: CXCL13+ CD8+ T cells
triplets.tail: Associated with favorable immunotherapy response across cancers; potential biomarker for ICI patient selection

triplets.head: Stem-like CD8+ T cells (TCF1+)
triplets.tail: TCF7, CD28, absence of TIM-3

triplets.head: Stem-like CD8+ T cells
triplets.tail: Self-renewing reservoir maintaining proliferative capacity; spatially localized near cDCs in specialized niches

triplets.head: Stem-like CD8+ T cell niches
triplets.tail: Supported by CXCL9, IL-15, CCL19/CCL21 crosstalk with cDCs, plus CXCR6 upregulation and epigenetic reprogramming

triplets.head: Stem-like CD8+ T cell niche presence
triplets.tail: Predicts ICB response; absence contributes to immune evasion

triplets.head: FLT3L and CD40 agonists
triplets.tail: Expand cDC1-stem-like T cell niches in preclinical models

triplets.head: CD8+ T cell exhaustion
triplets.tail: Tumor margin/stroma: TCF1+ stem-like progenitors; transition zone: GZMK+ intermediates; tumor core: TIM-3+/LAG-3+/ENTPD1+ terminally exhausted

triplets.head: CXCR6-CXCL16 axis
triplets.tail: CXCL16 on tumor cells attracts CD8+ T cells into malignant compartment; TCF7 represses CXCR6 keeping stem-like T cells near DCs

triplets.head: CXCR4-CXCL12 axis
triplets.tail: CXCL12 from desmoplastic fibroblasts retains T cells in stroma away from tumor cells

triplets.head: TREM2+ macrophages
triplets.tail: Identified by pan-cancer scRNA-seq atlas of myeloid cells

triplets.head: LAMP3+ DCs
triplets.tail: Identified by scRNA-seq; interact with Tregs via CCL17 in LN metastases

triplets.head: cDC1 (conventional DC type 1)
triplets.tail: Cross-present tumor antigens to CD8+ T cells; spatially co-localize with stem-like T cells; critical for anti-PD-1 response; abundance associated with CS macrophage polarity

triplets.head: TLS (Tertiary Lymphoid Structures)
triplets.tail: Core TLS (not peripheral) are most prognostic; in gastric cancer contain PD-1+TIM-3- CD8+ T cells correlating with improved survival

triplets.head: TLS
triplets.tail: In HCC, tumor-derived tryptophan metabolites impair TLS maturation - classified as immature conforming or deviating subtypes

triplets.head: TLS in RCC
triplets.tail: Function as sites of in situ B cell maturation; plasma cells migrate along CXCL12+ fibroblast tracks; IgG deposition on tumor cells correlates with apoptosis and ICI response

triplets.head: Perivascular niches
triplets.tail: Layered architecture around blood vessels: DCs and T cells near endothelium, macrophages at outer boundary; in GBM enriched with immunosuppressive macrophages and collagen-rich ECM

triplets.head: Immune-excluded niches
triplets.tail: Dense CAF-deposited ECM, CXCL12-CXCR4 misdirection, TGF-β signaling, CD47-THBS1 inhibitory interactions

triplets.head: Hypoxic niches
triplets.tail: In HCC, hypoxia induces SPP1+ TAMs that co-localize with CAFs driving immune exclusion; in GBM, layered structures with proinflammatory/immunosuppressive macrophages

triplets.head: Neuroimmune interface niches
triplets.tail: In PDAC, non-invaded nerves associate with TLS (immunosupportive); invaded nerves surrounded by NLRP3+ macrophages and myCAFs (immunosuppressive)

triplets.head: Microbiota-residing niches
triplets.tail: Bacteria-rich niches within tumors are spatially organized and highly immunosuppressive; higher bacterial burden in tumor cells than TME or normal tissue

triplets.head: Fusobacterium-residing niche
triplets.tail: Linked to cancer cell quiescence and chemoresistance

triplets.head: Tumor invasive front
triplets.tail: Leading-edge tumor cells show stem-like, hypoxic, therapy-resistant reprogramming; upregulate immune checkpoints; downregulate antigen presentation

triplets.head: subTMEs (sub-tumor microenvironments)
triplets.tail: Spatially distinct microenvironmental states co-existing within single tumors: reactive (higher immune infiltration) vs deserted (myxoid stroma, immune desert)

triplets.head: subTMEs
triplets.tail: Single biopsy may capture only one subTME and miss the other, explaining why biopsies can be misleading for predicting immunotherapy response

triplets.head: MTIL (Malignant TIL Program)
triplets.tail: 100-gene program in malignant cells that robustly predicts T cell infiltration; identified from 2.6 million cells across 130 HGSC tumors

triplets.head: MTIL program
triplets.tail: Predicted patient outcomes 5-8 years into the future from a single tissue sample; independent of BRCA status, TMB, age, disease stage

triplets.head: MTIL-up genes
triplets.tail: Antigen presentation, IFN-γ signaling, chemokines

triplets.head: MTIL-down genes
triplets.tail: Proliferation and stemness programs

triplets.head: MTIL program
triplets.tail: Shifting tumor cells toward MTIL-up state via IFN-γ induction, epigenetic drugs, or STING agonists could convert immune-excluded tumors to infiltrated

triplets.head: s1-s4 CAF organizational patterns
triplets.tail: Defined by neighboring cell composition rather than intrinsic markers in pan-cancer spatial multi-omics study by Liu et al.

triplets.head: s1-s4 CAF organizational patterns
triplets.tail: Four conserved spatial CAF patterns with distinct intercellular communication networks; CAF function determined more by spatial context than cell-intrinsic identity

triplets.head: CD80/CD86-CTLA4
triplets.tail: Suppressive monocyte-to-CD8+ T cell interaction in malignant compartment identified by spatial ligand-receptor analysis

triplets.head: TIM-3-Galectin-9 (LGALS9)
triplets.tail: Immune checkpoint active specifically at tumor-T cell interface; supports TIM-3 inhibitor development

triplets.head: CD47-THBS1
triplets.tail: Don't eat me signal reinforcing immune exclusion in immune-excluded niches; supports anti-CD47 targeting

triplets.head: SPP1-CD44/integrins
triplets.tail: SPP1+ macrophage-to-tumor/fibroblast signaling driving ECM remodeling, angiogenesis, immune exclusion

triplets.head: VEGFA-VEGFR
triplets.tail: VEGFA+ macrophage-to-endothelial cell signaling in perivascular niches driving angiogenesis (IMC in HCC)

triplets.head: CXCL13-CXCR5
triplets.tail: CXCL13+ CAFs/T cells-to-B cells promoting TLS formation; agonizing this axis could enhance TLS maturation

triplets.head: NRG1-ErbB
triplets.tail: Damaged axon-to-Schwann cell signaling in PDAC perineural niche; NRG1 blockade for perineural invasion

triplets.head: IL-15-IL-15R
triplets.tail: cDC-to-stem-like CD8+ T cell signaling sustaining stem-like pool; IL-15 superagonists to expand these niches

triplets.head: FLT3L-FLT3
triplets.tail: Stromal cell-to-cDC1 signaling expanding cDC1s and stem-like T cell niches; FLT3L therapy to reprogram cold tumors

triplets.head: Intratumoral three-cell-type clusters
triplets.tail: DCs commonly interact with both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells simultaneously within TME; a conserved feature across cancers

triplets.head: Spatial transcriptomics
triplets.tail: T/NK cells preferentially localized in stromal rather than malignant compartment; patients with higher T/NK abundance had improved outcomes

triplets.head: CD8 TIP (Tumor Infiltration Program)
triplets.tail: Gene program marking CD8+ T cells proximal to malignant cells: upregulates granzymes, perforin, CCL3/4/5, IFNG, checkpoints (CTLA4, HAVCR2, PDCD1, TIGIT, LAG3), CXCR6; downregulates naive markers (SELL, IL7R, TCF7, CXCR4)

triplets.head: Desmoplastic fibroblasts
triplets.tail: Upregulate CXCL12 and associate with T/NK cell-enriched niches; preferentially co-localize with naive and memory T cells rather than effector/exhausted T cells

triplets.head: Single-cell/spatial technologies
triplets.tail: Before: ~5-10 cell types in TME; After: 32+ T cell states, 7+ macrophage states, 5+ CAF subtypes, multiple DC states

triplets.head: Single-cell/spatial technologies
triplets.tail: Before: M1/M2 paradigm; After: CXCL9:SPP1 polarity axis which has prognostic value while M1/M2 markers do not

triplets.head: Single-cell/spatial technologies
triplets.relation: paradigm shift: T cell exhaustion understanding
triplets.tail: Before: single exhausted state; After: spatial gradient from stem-like to terminal governed by chemokine axes and DC proximity

triplets.head: Single-cell/spatial technologies
triplets.tail: Before: TME viewed as homogeneous per patient; After: subTMEs co-exist within single tumors making single biopsies misleading

triplets.head: Single-cell/spatial technologies
triplets.relation: paradigm shift: hot vs cold classification
triplets.tail: Before: binary hot/cold; After: nine+ functional niches with distinct compositions, communication networks, and therapeutic vulnerabilities

triplets.head: Single-cell/spatial technologies
triplets.tail: Before: single-molecule logic; After: communication network analysis reveals targetable intercellular signaling axes
